fields.subnational_unit: eight strategically selected South African municipalities across provinces (including Gauteng municipalities)
fields.population: South African municipal water services and municipalities audited by the Auditor-General (2015-2024)
fields.sample_size: 8 case municipalities (purposive); documentary sources: AGSA consolidated audit reports 2015-2024, SIU and SAHRC investigations, amaBhungane and Daily Maverick investigations, peer-reviewed literature
fields.effect_measure: critical governance / political-economy documentary analysis with triangulation across source types; critical discourse analysis, constitutional analysis, comparative case analysis
fields.effect_estimate: Water insecurity is attributed to infrastructure decay and corrupt procurement, a 'tanker-industrial complex' (R2.1 billion Gauteng tanker spending 2018-2023), cadre deployment and state-capture patronage, and weakened climate adaptation, reproducing 'hydraulic apartheid'. Background figures cited: 37% national non-revenue water (30-55% by province); maintenance budgets fell from 6.2% (2015) to 4.1% (2023); 26% of municipalities with clean audits (2023-24). Reform pathways: anticorruption enforcement, administrative professionalisation, financial management, possible restructuring of service delivery where municipal governance has failed. The author states the cases are illustrative, not representative, and that no primary community data were collected.
fields.study_design: perspective article: documentary analysis of eight purposively selected municipal cases
fields.section: Full text (Discover Water 6:53, open access, article type 'Perspective'): Abstract; Methodological approach 3.1-3.4; results; Conclusion

evidence_level: Perspective / documentary analysis: eight purposively selected South African municipal cases triangulated from auditor-general reports, investigative journalism and academic literature, read in full text 2026-10-04. Attributes water insecurity to governance failure, corruption and failed enforcement despite constitutional guarantees. The author acknowledges no primary data and non-representative cases; no effect estimates.
